colwyn bay.snapshot: Colwyn Bay sits on the North Wales coast where Openreach and the Welsh alt-nets are pushing full fibre out through the resort and its surrounding communities. The build and cabling trade here runs two ways: the fleets and build contractors order their workwear on trade accounts, while the ex-BT sole traders and one-van broadband and CCTV installers order direct online, with no account, whenever they need a few branded pieces.
colwyn bay.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Conwy
s1loc: Colwyn Bay is in the middle of the North Wales full-fibre build, with Openreach engineers running fibre out through the town and into Old Colwyn, Rhos-on-Sea, Mochdre and Llysfaen, and the Welsh alt-nets including Ogi extending their footprint across Conwy alongside the wider Project Gigabit programme reaching the harder coastal and rural premises. Virgin Media and the mobile operators keep upgrading on top. Around that build sit local broadband, CCTV and structured-cabling installers, and a long tail of subcontractors and ex-BT sole traders taking on connection work across the resort and its outlying villages.

Alongside the residential rollout sits a commercial scene. Mochdre Business Park off Swan Road and the trade units toward Glan Conwy give the area its structured-cabling and fibre-optic work, wiring offices, schools and multi-site businesses in Cat5e, Cat6 and fibre across Conwy. CCTV installers cover the seafront, the town centre and the retail and industrial units, while cabling firms serve the hospitality, holiday and care premises that line the coast from Llanddulas through to Rhos-on-Sea. It is a steady mix of network, broadband and security work spread across the town and its neighbouring communities.
